channel.title: HANTANG 한탕 — Jjimjilbang & Korean Bathhouse Guide
channel.description: Find a jjimjilbang, Korean sauna or bathhouse anywhere in Korea: 5,600+ places with map links, tattoo rules, prices, body scrub (seshin) and etiquette — in your language.

item.title: Your first tang, step by step — HANTANG
item.description: The whole visit in order, from the shoe locker to the checkout counter, with what to say and what to do at the three moments where first-timers freeze.

item.title: Mogyoktang, sauna, jjimjilbang, hanjeungmak, oncheon: which is which — HANTANG
item.description: Six Korean words for a place to bathe or sweat, one legal category. What each kind of place has and lacks, what it costs, how to spot it, and which to pick for your plan.

item.title: The unwritten rules — HANTANG
item.description: Every rule of the Korean bath, grouped by where you are standing, with the reason behind each one, what happens if you break it, and the few rules that are actually law.

item.title: Tattoos in Korean saunas: the real rules — HANTANG
item.description: No Korean law bans tattoos in a bath. Refusals and cover-up rules are house policy, written down mostly by hotel pools and saunas. What is documented, what is hearsay, and what to do.

item.title: Seshin, explained — HANTANG
item.description: The Korean full-body scrub, from the Italy towel to the table: what happens, what it costs in 2025–26, how to ask for gentle or hard, and who should skip it.

item.title: Inside: every pool and room explained — HANTANG
item.description: Pool by pool and room by room: the temperatures that have been published, what each wall is claimed to do and what is actually known, how long to stay, and a rotation that works.

item.title: Sikhye, eggs and banana milk — HANTANG
item.description: What the jjimjilbang snack counter sells, how the three classic items got there, what they cost in 2026 and how to order them on your wristband.

item.title: What it costs, when it opens, what to bring — HANTANG
item.description: Admission by type of bath and city, with dates. What is included, what costs extra, hours and closing days, night rates and time limits, and a packing list.

item.title: Sleeping overnight in a jjimjilbang — HANTANG
item.description: A night on a heated floor for about ₩14,000–20,000 in Seoul. Which Seoul and Busan places still allow it in 2026, how the night runs, what it costs, and who should book a hotel instead.

item.title: Heat, cold and your body — HANTANG
item.description: How long to stay in, when to get out, who should not go in at all, and which of the health claims on the wall have evidence behind them. From Korean officials, clinicians and the sauna research.

item.title: Kids, families, women and special situations — HANTANG
item.description: The age limit for children in the opposite-sex bath, how families split and meet, women-only venues, accessibility, modesty, LGBTQ+ visitors, periods, scars and older travelers.

item.title: 40 bathhouse phrases and the signs you'll see — HANTANG
item.description: Every phrase from the HANTANG game, grouped by where you will use it, plus the signs on the wall, what the counter may ask you, and how the polite -yo ending works.

item.title: A short history of the Korean bath — HANTANG
item.description: From Joseon sweat houses and the first public bathhouses to the jjimjilbang boom and today's closures. How Korea came to bathe together, and why to see the neighborhood tang now.

item.title: Where to go: Seoul, Busan and the hot-spring towns — HANTANG
item.description: Seoul's baths cluster around Dongdaemun, Myeongdong and Hongdae; Busan adds hot springs and seawater beside the beach; six old spa towns are a train or bus ride away. What is open, what has closed, and what each is worth.

item.title: Jjimjilbang & Korean Bathhouse Directory: All 5,640 Places
item.description: Search 5,640 licensed jjimjilbangs, saunas, bathhouses and scrub shops across Korea by name, district or distance, with map links, directions and a taxi card in Korean.

item.title: Jjimjilbang & Saunas near Myeongdong, Hongdae, Haeundae and More
item.description: Find a jjimjilbang, Korean bathhouse or sauna near your hotel: 25 areas in Seoul, Busan, Jeju and beyond, sorted by distance with Google Maps, Naver Map and Kakao Map links.

item.title: Top-Rated Korean Bathhouses & Jjimjilbang (2026) — HANTANG
item.description: 11 Korean bathhouses, spas and scrub shops that many visitors rate highly on Google Maps, Kakao Map and booking sites. Nobody can pay to be listed.

item.title: Korean Hot Spring Towns & Free Foot Baths — HANTANG
item.description: Korea’s hot spring towns — Onyang, Yuseong, Suanbo, Bugok, Baegam, Deoksan — and free public foot baths: water, hours and how to get there.

item.title: Private Korean Baths & One-Person Scrub Rooms — HANTANG
item.description: Private bath rooms, solo saunas and one-person Korean body scrub (seshin) shops in Seoul, Busan and beyond: prices, session length and how to book.
